clauses.reason: Executive Order 7946 (August 9, 1938; 3 FR 1965) limits the quantity of red cedar shingles imported from Canada that may be admitted to entry during the last six months of the calendar year 1938 to 864,881 squares, under section 811 of the Revenue Act of 1936. The clause's own wording confines the limit to that period, so the limit expired when the last six months of 1938 ended. I record the end as December 31, 1938 inclusive (the limit runs through that day); the exclusive reading is that it ended when January 1, 1939 began. Executive Order 8051 of February 15, 1939 (4 FR 959), which this packet holds as the later order for the next half-year, recites that Executive Orders 7701, 7822 and 7946 covered the periods July 1, 1937 to December 31, 1937, January 1, 1938 to June 30, 1938 and July 1, 1938 to December 31, 1938, which confirms the reading of the period; it does not act on EO 7946. The dossier lead ACT:EO:7946>EO:8051 (verb 'terminate') is the sentence in EO 8051 that ends EO 8051 itself on termination of the 1935 Canadian trade agreement; it does not revoke or end EO 7946, so it is not an end of this order. No earlier end is held.

research_rationale:
EO 7946 (Limiting the Importation of Red Cedar Shingles From Canada During the Last Six Months of 1938; 3 FR 1965) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It is a one-period import quota, so its only clause ended by its own terms on December 31, 1938 and the whole order is not in force on 2026-10-14. The status decision for this member records 'no'. The catalog observation for EO 7946 has an empty note, which establishes nothing about current effect; the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) found no later instrument that amends, revokes or extends it.

savings.reason: EO 7946 contains no savings clause. Entries admitted within the 864,881-square limit before the period closed were completed acts, and no held source preserves any right, duty or proceeding under the limit after December 31, 1938.
